text: Write a story called No Way Out, about a person who is trying to find a way out of a difficult
situation. In your writing, create a sense of tension and drama.
Write two contrasting diary entries (300–450 words each) about a competition: the first by a person
who did better than they had expected in the competition; the second by another person, who did
not do as well as they had expected. In your writing, create a sense of mood and reflection.
Write a descriptive piece about the evening rush hour in a city. In your writing, focus on sound,
movement and colour to help your reader imagine the scene.
Section B: Writing for an audience
In class, you have been discussing what it means to be an adult. Write an article for your school
magazine, focusing on the roles and responsibilities that people gain as they reach adulthood,
and how adulthood changes a person’s outlook and character.
A newspaper recently published an article saying that in the near future cash will no longer be
used, and all payments will be made electronically. Readers were invited to respond to this article.
Write two contrasting letters (300–450 words each): one positive about a future cashless society,
and the other negative about the idea.
Your headteacher has asked you to give a talk to students at your school about the benefits of
visiting other countries. Write the text for your talk. In your writing, focus on how travel broadens
the mind, and what people can learn from visiting other countries.
